From the mixed-to-same-shore one-hop block W, the Gram entry counts for two mixed states are m+n−2 at equality, m if only their first-shore coordinate agrees, n if only the second agrees, and 2 otherwise. Resolving the shore constants and their orthogonal complements gives the stated three positive squared frequencies and one zero sector. Their basis-state weights are as claimed. An independent integer check computed five positive diagonal Gram moments by counting common same-shore neighbors directly for (3,3), (3,5), (4,6), and all agreed. The grading J=+1 on mixed states and −1 otherwise anticommutes with H, hence 1−2P(t) is the real return amplitude at time 2t. In the balanced case both positive sine-square coefficients are nonzero; equality requires both terms to be one. The ratio 2√((r−1)/(r−2)) is irrational, since a rational square-root ratio of coprime positive integers requires both to be squares and consecutive positive squares are impossible. Fixing the second phase at π/2 modulo π leaves the first phase following an irrational rotation; the nonnegative orbit is dense. This proves both sharpness and finite-time nonattainment, with t=0 automatically excluded. The short-time illustration and unit-rate exclusion solution remain correct supporting comparisons, not new claims. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.
